$comment: VALE client layer (CONTRACT §4 ClientDef, §10). nav = the six top-level screens (icons: assets/ui/icons/nav/<id>.svg, UI icon lane). modeSlots = the Mode Dial in order: RIFT, BRIDGE, FRAY, then the reserved 'uncarved hour' (WORLD §3: a designed tile, carved by adding a record here). home = headline + feature + tiles; screen ids and params are documented in _design/sections/client_hud.md §2. menuScene = the Rim at the Split Hour (STYLE_BIBLE Menu mood). tips = loading-screen and idle tips, WORLD tone, every number checked against modes.json / queues.json / team_buffs.json. A tip led by a mode tag, '[rift] ' or '[rift,bridge] ' (mode ids), shows only on those modes' loading screens and the tag is never shown; an untagged tip is true on every mode (loading:tip-mode).

modeSlots.label: The uncarved hour
modeSlots.note: A new mode will be cut here.

home.headline: Long light on the Vale
home.sub: Pick a mode, take your side of the dial, and fight for the hour you want to keep.

feature.title: Three roads, one Hourbell
feature.body: Draft five fighters, hold the Dialwood and silence the enemy Hourbell on Hourfall. Matches run about 25 minutes.

tiles.title: Ranked season
tiles.body: Opens at account level 20. Five placement matches set your rank.

tiles.title: Skins in the shop
tiles.body: Spend the Candles you earn on new looks for your fighters.

tiles.title: Sparring practice
tiles.body: Any fighter, the full map, alone. Add Gleam and levels, reset cooldowns.

tiles.title: Your collection
tiles.body: Every fighter is free. Skins change how they look, never how they play.

tips: [rift,bridge] By default, allies glow azure and enemies glow marigold on every map. Settings let you change both.
A glow on an enemy fighter is a warning. When their light flares, an ability is on its way.
Enemy danger areas are brightest at the edge. Step out before the circle closes.
Hold the scoreboard key to see every fighter's items and levels. Let go and it closes.
[rift] Unspent Gleam fights for no one. Recall when you can afford a full item.
[rift] Recall takes about 7 s. Start it somewhere an enemy cannot reach in that time.
Needlegrass hides you from enemies outside it. An enemy standing in the same grass can still see you.
[rift,bridge] A Needle's shadow ring shows how far it can strike. Stay outside it unless you mean to break it.
[rift] A Needle's shadow ring turns aside your blows unless your own Wicks stand in it. Bring the wave.
[rift] Until 7:00 every Outer Needle wears a Dawn Seal that re-sets every 30 s: one wave won't crack it, a stacked wave will.
[rift] Grove tithe: while your Grovehunter trails your team's lead, each camp monster pays it extra XP from what your lanes earned.
[rift,bridge] A Lantern holds a road's stored light. When it falls, your team gains Lanternwake until it relights 4:00 later.
[rift] The Glasshorn gives your whole team Clearglass for 90 s: faster cooldowns and quicker Light regeneration while you stand on your own side of the Noonline.
[rift] The Resinback gives your team Resinburn for 90 s. On the enemy side of the Noonline, an attack sticks resin to its target and your next attack ignites it.
[rift] Each Sunsplinter you take adds a Splinter for your team. Longshade, late in the match, gives the living team the Long Shade for sieging.
[rift,bridge] Your ultimate unlocks at level 6, then ranks up at levels 11 and 16.
[bridge] BRIDGE has no recall. Take the Mending Sunmotes that fall on the span, and shop at home, beside your own standing Needles, or while you wait to return.
[bridge] In BRIDGE, you can take one fighter from your team's Lot; yours goes there for a teammate. The Lot burns down one fighter every 8 s.
[bridge] At 21:00 the Gorge Wind rises: nothing loses its protection, but every 45 s the waves hit harder and the Needles wear thin.
[fray] FRAY gives you four lives. First to 12 takedowns or the last one standing wins, and the Hour Board ranks the rest.
[fray] The Lampwright cart on the Noonplate is shared by all ten. Shop between fights, not during them.
[fray] From 8:00 the Noon Toll rings every 20 s and shows every fighter to everyone for 5 s. Late in the match, nobody stays hidden.
Physical damage numbers are chalk and magic damage numbers are orchid-rose. Armor shrinks the first, resist the second.
Numerals in ink with a pale halo are damage that ignores armor and resist.
[rift,bridge] Pings are how your team talks. Say what you see before the fight, not during it.
After a fall, the recap lists the damage you took in the last 15 s. Read it once, then carry on.
Your first win of each day pays a bonus on top of the usual Candles.
[rift] Ranked opens at account level 20. Until then, Quick and Draft are the places to learn.
Quick cast fires an ability the moment you press its key. Turn it on under Settings, Controls.
Colorblind modes change the ally and enemy colors and add a shape to each. Find them under Settings, Accessibility.
